raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: Saprophytic aspergillosis (aspergilloma) classically presents as a mobile fungal ball within a pre-existing cavity (often from prior TB), appearing as a round soft tissue mass separated from the cavity wall by an air crescent. This specific radiographic sign distinguishes it from simple cavities, fluid levels, or calcified masses.
